title: Lipschitz stability of integrals in $L^2$
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $U,V\in L^2(\mu)$. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then
\[
\left|\int_\Omega\psi(U)\,d\mu-\int_\Omega\psi(V)\,d\mu\right|\le c\,N_2(U-V),
\]
where $N_2$ denotes the real-valued random-variable norm at exponent $2$.
hypotheses_covered: A function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ that is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$
